Be a catalyst for innovation with a master’s or Ph.D. in chemical engineering
At Oregon State University, you’ll find a collaborative atmosphere with rigorous academics and world-changing innovation. Whether you pursue a master’s in chemical engineering, a Master of Engineering degree, or a Ph.D. in chemical engineering, Oregon State is the perfect setting for you to explore solutions for better products, healthier people, and a more sustainable environment.
You’ll work alongside our diverse faculty pursuing a variety of research interests, with concentrations of expertise in surface chemistry/catalysis, reaction engineering, and computational modeling/simulation. Current research includes projects in renewable energy, microreactors, advanced sensors, nanoparticles, semiconductors, and smart surfaces.

Graduate Program Details
How to Apply
How to Apply
Confirm You Meet the Minimum Academic Requirements.
Every student must meet a set of academic requirements to be admitted to any graduate program at Oregon State.
Domestic applicants: Confirm you meet the minimum academic requirements for graduate school at Oregon State.
International applicants must meet the minimum requirements for international applicants.
Apply Online.
Prospective graduate students may access the OSU Graduate Programs application online. The application will walk you through submitting all the required materials and paying your fee.
M.S. and Ph.D. Application
M.Eng. Application (Domestic Applicants)
M.Eng. Application (International Applicants)
Gather Your Transcripts.
Provide transcripts from all institutions where coursework was completed or attempted in pursuit of an undergraduate or graduate degree.
This includes, for example, coursework completed at a community college and later transferred to a four-year institution and counted toward a bachelor’s degree.
During the application process, we accept unofficial or official transcripts.
If you are admitted to OSU and you applied using unofficial transcripts, you will need to send official transcripts to the Office of Graduate Education. When ready to send official transcripts, please send electronic transcripts from the U.S. institutions you attended. When ordering a transcript as part of your graduate admissions record, select “Oregon State University-Graduate Admissions” as the recipient.
Request Three Letters of Recommendation. (MS. & Ph.D. applicants only)
A letter of recommendation is a written document from a professor, supervisor, or other non-family individual who can speak to your academic or research successes/potential, character and/or leadership qualities, overall progress, and/or other achievements.
As part of the application for admission, you will provide the names and email addresses of three people to write you a letter of recommendation (or “letter of reference”). The letter of reference system triggers an email to each reference writer and enables them to submit a confidential electronic letter for you.
Ask the people you’d like to be your letter writers before you list them on an application. Explain what program you are applying for and why you are interested in pursuing graduate school. This will help them gauge what to highlight in the letter. Clarify the deadline and let them know to expect an email with submission instructions. The OSU Office of Graduate Education has additional helpful suggestions.
Write a Statement of Objectives. (M.S. & Ph.D. applicants only).
In a one-page statement, outline your motivations for pursuing graduate study, your academic and professional goals, and why our specific program is a good fit for you.
The application includes the question/prompt, “Compose a statement of academic and career objectives. Please be as specific as possible about your proposed focus of study. You should address your motivations for graduate study and briefly explain your overall preparation to enter your chosen field.” This is where your personal statement/statement of objectives should go, and does not need to be uploaded as a separate document.
The M.S. and Ph.D. applications include a few supplemental questions, intended to get to know you better, beyond the confines of the statement of objectives. Use these questions to highlight aspects of your story that may not be reflected in other parts of the application.
Identify Faculty of Interest (M.S. & Ph.D. applicants only).
All funded incoming M.S. and Ph.D. students will be matched with a faculty advisor when admitted into the program.
The application allows you to list faculty with whom you are most interested in working if you were to be accepted into the program. Explore our research areas and our individual faculty pages to identify faculty whose work interests you.
You do not need to secure a faculty advisor before applying to the program. Faculty who are recruiting students will review applications in our applicant pool. While not required, you can feel free to reach out to potential faculty of interest directly, though some prefer to wait until applications are received to consider your materials/interest. Don’t worry if you don’t hear back from email outreach.
Prepare Your CV/Resume.
A curriculum vitae (CV) is a detailed document outlining your academic background, research experience, publications, awards, and scholarly achievements.
Upload your CV or resume when prompted in the online application.
International Students: Provide Test Scores.
Provide the Office of Graduate Education a score report on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS).
The Office of Graduate Education's English proficiency requirements for admission are listed on their website, with particular requirements concerning Graduate Teaching Assistants (GTAs). Explore the English proficiency requirements.
Pay the Application Fee.
A non-refundable application fee is required for each application you submit. Visit the Office of Graduate Education website for the current fees.
Our program does not provide application fee waivers. If you are a domestic applicant, the Office of Graduate Education may grant an application fee waiver to applicants who meet specific criteria.
After Applying: Check Your Application Status.
You may check your application status at any time by signing in to the application portal. You will need the email address and password you used when completing the application.
You will be notified by email to check the application portal when an admission decision has been made.
Graduate applications sometimes remain in "Review" status for many weeks. Our program usually reviews files at scheduled intervals, not daily.
When to apply
Deadlines
Students must apply by the deadline. There is no separate funding application; funding consideration is automatic.
Final deadline for M.S. and Ph.D. applications: January 5
Final deadline for MENG applications: May 1

Admissions Process
Admissions Process
When are applications reviewed?
Ph.D. and M.S. applicants are reviewed once the final deadline has passed.
Application decisions begin in February and continue through Spring, but the decision process may extend later in some circumstances.
MENG applications are generally reviewed on a rolling basis as they are submitted.
Who reviews applications and makes admission decisions?
All applicants are reviewed by a minimum of two faculty members of the corresponding program. Programs will meet and do a secondary review of those students of interest to admit to the program.
Following the program's recommendation, OSU Graduate Admissions will determine whether the general university admission requirements have been met and will issue the formal admission.
Applicants are evaluated on their entire application, and admission decisions are made based on the strength of each application relative to the applicant pool in any given year. Meeting the minimum application requirements does not guarantee admission.
PhD/MS admission decisions are based on many factors, such as the quality of the applicant’s prior academic degree and record of accomplishment, statement of objectives, letters of recommendation from professors or others familiar with the applicant’s academic work, relevant work experience, preparation in the proposed field of study, funding availability from faculty, and the suitability of the applicant’s academic goals with the faculty’s research interests. A critical consideration is whether Oregon State's graduate programs can satisfactorily fulfill your academic objectives.
Application Tips
Start early
Give yourself time to research our program, prepare application materials, and request letters of recommendation.
Apply by the deadline
Applications will not be reviewed after the deadline has passed.
Be strategic
Tailor your statement of purpose to our program and highlight why you think we are a good fit for your interests.
Seek guidance
Reach out to your mentors, your professors, or others who have gone through the process to get advice and feedback on your application materials.
Assistantships and Fellowships
Assistantships and Fellowships
The School of Chemical, Biological, and Environmental Engineering offers a limited number of graduate teaching assistantships (GTA) and graduate research assistantships (GRA). There is no separate application process. Students whose applications are complete by the deadline are automatically considered for available GTA/GRA positions. Funding is prioritized for PhD applicants. M.S. students may be admitted on a self-funded basis.
Graduate teaching assistants and research assistants are appointed on a term-by-term basis. They receive tuition remission and a monthly stipend.
Fellowships are also available to incoming graduate students with a monthly stipend for the nine-month academic year. Typically, one to two fellowships are awarded per academic year. There is no separate application process for fellowships; qualified graduate applicants to the department are automatically considered for available fellowships.
Funding Offers
At times, funding offers are made at the same time you have received the admission decision. Sometimes, admission decisions and funding offers are staggered, with the admission decision made before the potential funding offer. Whenever there are updates to your application status/funding status, you will be notified to check the application portal.
Accept your funding offer by April 15. This deadline for accepting financial support is set by OSU and many CGS member institutions; further admission/funding offers may be issued shortly after that date.
You may be admitted as a graduate student without an offer of funding. This is typically more common with MS students. The MEng degree is not eligible for GTA/GRA funding support.
*Award offers and amounts are subject to change at the discretion of department administrators.
Master of Science Requirements
Master of Science Requirements
The student’s M.S. program of study shall be designed to develop a degree of competence in the major area significantly higher than the customary baccalaureate education, and shall include background and adjunct knowledge normally expected of a person entering the professional practice of that specialty.
View Requirements
Master of Engineering Requirements
Master of Engineering Requirements
Strengthen your technical credentials with a Master of Engineering
The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professional, coursework-only degree designed for individuals seeking practical skills and leadership roles in industry. The program does not require a thesis or research project, allowing students to focus on advanced coursework aligned with their professional goals and job-related skill development.
MEng vs. M.S. Degrees
The Master of Science (M.S.) degree is research-oriented and suited for students interested in advanced technical research or pursuing a Ph.D., typically requiring a thesis or research project. In contrast, the MEng is a course-based degree intended for students who want to apply advanced engineering knowledge in industry without completing a thesis. Read more about the difference between an MEng and an MS degree.
Learn about MEng vs M.S.
MEng Degree Requirements
Oregon State’s MEng program requires 45 credits of advanced coursework, which may include core engineering courses, ethics, technical writing, and elective courses relevant to professional interests. Students typically develop a Program of Study with an advisor during their first term and complete a final portfolio in place of a final oral exam.
View detailed MEng requirements
Paying for your MEng
MEng students are generally self-funded. While all students may apply for graduate research or teaching assistantships, these opportunities are highly competitive and more commonly awarded to Ph.D. and M.S. students. Additional funding options include scholarships, grants, fellowships, loans, and employer tuition reimbursement programs. Learn more about paying for your MEng degree.
Explore MEng payment options
How to Apply
Apply to a Master of Engineering program online through the Office of Graduate Education. MEng degree admission requirements basically align with the minimum academic requirements for admission into all Oregon State graduate programs. This typically looks like having a four-year baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university with a cumulative B average. The GRE is not required for admission to an MEng degree.
Deadlines
The chemical engineering MEng program admits students for a fall term start date.
Application deadline: May 1
Apply Now
Ph.D. Degree Requirements
Ph.D. Degree Requirements
The purpose of the courses in the Ph.D. program of study is to develop exceptional expertise in the major area. It should also provide the background and adjunct knowledge required to practice and/or teach this specialty at the highest professional level and to conduct significant research in this field. The Ph.D. thesis shall make an original and significant contribution to engineering knowledge.
View Requirements
Graduate Minor Requirements
Graduate Minor Requirements
The Graduate Minor in Chemical Engineering is for masters and doctoral level students who seek additional formal training and mentoring in chemical engineering. Students pursuing a Minor in Chemical Engineering must include at least one Chemical Engineering faculty member on their committee. This faculty member must be engaged in the development of the student’s Program of Study and in the case of Doctoral students, their dissertation research; therefore, it is recommended that this faculty member be identified early in the doctoral program.
